title: Academic Writing: Common Sentence Patterns, Part Four
titleZh: 学术写作：常用句型，第四部分
credits: John Russell wrote this story for Learning English. George Grow was the editor.

sentences.en: English has many patterns.
sentences.zh: 英语有许多句型。

sentences.en: Learning and mastering these patterns can help you improve your writing and speaking skills.
sentences.zh: 学习和掌握这些句型有助于提升你的写作和口语能力。

sentences.en: They can also help you do better on your next grammar test!
sentences.zh: 它们还能帮你在下一次语法测试中取得更好的成绩！

sentences.en: Today, we explore a common verb pattern: the transitive verb pattern.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们来探讨一种常见的动词句型：及物动词句型。

sentences.en: This pattern is common in writing, speaking, and even on language tests, such as the Test of English as a Foreign Language, or TOEFL.
sentences.zh: 这种句型在写作、口语中，甚至像"美国外语水平考试"（TOEFL）这样的语言测试中都很常见。

sentences.en: To get you started thinking about transitive verbs, consider this stanza from "Preface to a Twenty Volume Suicide Note," by the famous author Amiri Baraka.
sentences.zh: 为了帮助你开始思考及物动词，请看著名作家阿米里·巴拉卡《二十卷自杀笔记序言》中的这一节诗。

sentences.en: And now, each night I count the stars.
sentences.zh: 如今，每个夜晚我都数着星星。

sentences.en: And each night I get the same number.
sentences.zh: 每个夜晚我都数出相同的数目。

sentences.en: And when they will not come to be counted, I count the holes they leave.
sentences.zh: 当它们不肯来被点数时，我就数它们留下的空洞。

sentences.en: By the end of this story, you will understand one transitive verb pattern that Baraka uses in this stanza.
sentences.zh: 到这个故事结束时，你将理解巴拉卡在这一节诗中所用的一种及物动词句型。

sentences.en: In a previous Everyday Grammar, we discussed intransitive verbs.
sentences.zh: 在之前的"每日语法"中，我们讨论过不及物动词。

sentences.en: One feature of intransitive verbs is that they do not require a complement.
sentences.zh: 不及物动词的一个特点是，它们不需要补语。

sentences.en: In other words, there does not need to be a noun phrase or adjective to the right of the verb in the sentence.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，句子中动词右侧不必有名词短语或形容词。

sentences.en: Unlike intransitive verbs, transitive verbs take one or more complements.
sentences.zh: 与不及物动词不同，及物动词需要一个或多个补语。

sentences.en: Complements, in this case, refer to nouns or noun phrases that are immediately to the right of the verb in the sentence.
sentences.zh: 在这里，补语指的是句子中紧邻动词右侧的名词或名词短语。

sentences.en: There are several types of transitive verbs, but they all have one thing in common: a direct object.
sentences.zh: 及物动词有几种类型，但它们都有一个共同点：直接宾语。

sentences.en: In its most basic form, the direct object is the noun phrase that follows a transitive verb.
sentences.zh: 在最基本的形式中，直接宾语是紧跟在及物动词之后的名词短语。

sentences.en: A noun phrase is a noun and all the words and phrases that describe it.
sentences.zh: 名词短语由一个名词及描述它的所有词语和短语构成。

sentences.en: The basic transitive verb pattern is this:
sentences.zh: 基本的及物动词句型如下：

sentences.en: Transitive verbs are often – but by no means always! – action words.
sentences.zh: 及物动词往往是——但绝非总是——表示动作的词。

sentences.en: One way to know if the noun phrase is a direct object is if it is the receiver of the action of the verb.
sentences.zh: 判断名词短语是否为直接宾语的一种方法是看它是否是动词动作的承受者。

sentences.en: For example,
sentences.zh: 例如，

sentences.en: You can tell that the softball is receiving the action, hit.
sentences.zh: 你可以看出，垒球正是承受"击打"这个动作的对象。

sentences.en: However, the direct object does not always have to be the receiver of an action.
sentences.zh: 然而，直接宾语并不总是某个动作的承受者。

sentences.en: Consider this sentence:
sentences.zh: 看看这个句子：

sentences.en: My family enjoyed the concert
sentences.zh: 我的家人欣赏了那场音乐会。

sentences.en: In this sentence, it is hard to say that the direct object, the concert, is really receiving an action.
sentences.zh: 在这个句子中，很难说直接宾语"音乐会"真的承受了某个动作。

sentences.en: So, this leads us to another way to think of the direct object.
sentences.zh: 因此，这引导我们换一种思路来理解直接宾语。

sentences.en: It is the answer to a what or whom question.
sentences.zh: 它就是针对"什么"或"谁"这一问题的答案。

sentences.en: Consider these examples:
sentences.zh: 看看下面的例子：

sentences.en: Dirty laundry covered (what?) the bedroom floor.
sentences.zh: 脏衣服堆满了（什么？）卧室的地板。

sentences.en: We enjoyed (what?) the concert.
sentences.zh: 我们欣赏了（什么？）那场音乐会。

sentences.en: The teacher helped (whom?) her student.
sentences.zh: 老师帮助了（谁？）她的学生。

sentences.en: Once again, asking the what or whom question will not work all of the time, but it can be a useful strategy to help you recognize the direct object.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，提出"什么"或"谁"的问题并不能在所有情况下都奏效，但它是一种有用的策略，能帮助你识别直接宾语。

sentences.en: So, if it can be difficult to find the direct object, how can you tell if a verb is transitive?
sentences.zh: 因此，如果要找出直接宾语相当困难，那么如何判断一个动词是不是及物动词呢？

sentences.en: There are two reliable ways to check:
sentences.zh: 有两种可靠的方法可以检验：

sentences.en: One reliable way to test if a verb is transitive is to change it to the passive voice.
sentences.zh: 检验一个动词是否为及物动词的可靠方法是把它改为被动语态。

sentences.en: Think back to the example sentence, Mary hit the softball.
sentences.zh: 回想一下前面的例句：玛丽打了那个垒球。

sentences.en: If you change it to the passive voice, the sentence would be, The softball was hit by Mary.
sentences.zh: 如果把它改为被动语态，句子就会变成：那个垒球被玛丽打了。

sentences.en: If you can change the sentence from active to passive voice, then the verb is probably transitive.
sentences.zh: 如果你能把句子从主动语态改为被动语态，那么这个动词大概就是及物动词。

sentences.en: You can read more about the passive voice in a previous Everyday Grammar story.
sentences.zh: 你可以在之前的《日常语法》文章中了解更多关于被动语态的内容。

sentences.en: A second way to check if a verb is transitive is to think about the two noun phrases surrounding a verb.
sentences.zh: 判断一个动词是否为及物动词的另一种方法是，思考动词两侧的两个名词短语。

sentences.en: This strategy, say Robert Funk and Martha Kolln, two English grammar experts, is the best way to identify a transitive verb.
sentences.zh: 两位英语语法专家罗伯特·芳克和玛莎·科伦指出，这一策略是识别及物动词的最佳方法。

sentences.en: Here is the basic idea: If the two noun phrases refer to different things, then you know the verb is transitive.*
sentences.zh: 基本思路如下：如果这两个名词短语指代不同的事物，那么你就知道这个动词是及物动词。*

sentences.en: Think back to the sentence, Mary hit the softball.
sentences.zh: 回想一下那句句子：玛丽打了那个垒球。

sentences.en: The subject, Mary, refers to one thing, while the direct object, the softball, refers to a different thing.
sentences.zh: 主语玛丽指代一件事物，而直接宾语那个垒球指代另一件事物。

sentences.en: In technical terms, you could say the two noun phrases have different referents.
sentences.zh: 从专业术语来说，你可以说这两个名词短语有不同的指代对象。

sentences.en: Contrast this to a pattern we discussed in a previous Everyday Grammar: the BE pattern.
sentences.zh: 与之形成对比的，是我们之前在《日常语法》中讨论过的一种结构：be动词结构。

sentences.en: We gave an example sentence from Christina Aguilera's song.
sentences.zh: 我们曾举过克里斯蒂娜·阿奎莱拉歌曲中的一句例句。

sentences.en: She sings "I am beautiful."
sentences.zh: 她唱道："我很美。"

sentences.en: In that sentence, the word beautiful, the subject complement, refers to the subject, "I."
sentences.zh: 在那句歌词中，表语beautiful指代主语"我"。

sentences.en: They refer to the same person - that is, they have the same referent.
sentences.zh: 它们指代同一个人——也就是说，它们有相同的指代对象。

sentences.en: In English, words that come after a verb often give information about the verb.
sentences.zh: 在英语中，位于动词之后的词往往提供关于该动词的信息。

sentences.en: Looking at what comes after a verb can really help you figure out the meaning of a verb, even if you do not know it.
sentences.zh: 观察动词之后的内容，确实能帮助你理解一个动词的含义，即使你并不认识它。

sentences.en: Now, think back to the stanza of Amiri Baraka's poem:
sentences.zh: 现在，回想一下阿米里·巴拉卡的诗中的这一节：

sentences.en: And now, each night I count the stars.
sentences.zh: 如今，每个夜晚我都数着星星。

sentences.en: And each night I get the same number.
sentences.zh: 每个夜晚我都得到相同的数目。

sentences.en: And when they will not come to be counted, I count the holes they leave.
sentences.zh: 当它们不肯前来被数时，我便数它们留下的空洞。

sentences.en: You can see the transitive verb pattern clearly in this stanza.
sentences.zh: 在这节诗中，你可以清楚地看到及物动词的结构。

sentences.en: Consider the first line:
sentences.zh: 来看第一行：

sentences.en: And now, each night I count the stars.
sentences.zh: 而现在，每个夜晚我都会数着星星。

sentences.en: Baraka starts the line with adverbial information,** and then uses the basic transitive verb pattern:
sentences.zh: Baraka用状语信息开始这一行，**然后使用基本的及物动词结构：

sentences.en: How do you know the verb is transitive?
sentences.zh: 你怎么知道这个动词是及物的呢？

sentences.en: You could try asking a what question:
sentences.zh: 你可以尝试提出一个针对"什么"的问题：

sentences.en: I count (what?) the stars.
sentences.zh: 我数（什么？）星星。

sentences.en: Or you could even change the sentence passive voice:
sentences.zh: 或者你甚至可以改变句子的被动语态：

sentences.en: I count the stars.
sentences.zh: 我数着星星。

sentences.en: The stars were counted by me.
sentences.zh: 星星被我数着。

sentences.en: A third option is to ask yourself what the noun phrases around the verb refer to.
sentences.zh: 第三种方法是问你自己动词周围的名词短语指的是什么。

sentences.en: You know it is transitive because the subject, "I," refers to a person, while the direct object, "the stars," refers to something different from a person.
sentences.zh: 你知道它是及物的，因为主语"我"指的是一个人，而直接宾语"星星"指的是不同于人的事物。

sentences.en: The second line, like the first line, uses a similar structure:
sentences.zh: 第二行与第一行一样，使用了类似的结构：

sentences.en: The remaining two lines in the stanza use structures that are more complex than the basic transitive verb pattern.
sentences.zh: 诗节中剩下的两行使用了比基本及物动词结构更复杂的结构。

sentences.en: However, you can still see that writers can use basic patterns to create beautiful poetry.
sentences.zh: 不过，你仍然可以看到作者如何使用基本结构来创作出优美的诗歌。

sentences.en: To practice using transitive verb patterns, you can write a poem similar to Baraka's poem.
sentences.zh: 为了练习使用及物动词结构，你可以写一首类似Baraka的诗歌。

sentences.en: Be sure to choose new transitive verbs and new noun phrases that act as the direct object.
sentences.zh: 一定要选择新的及物动词和充当直接宾语的新名词短语。

sentences.en: Write your poems in the comments section or on our Facebook page.
sentences.zh: 把你的诗写在评论区或者我们的Facebook页面上。

sentences.en: I'm Jill Robbins.
sentences.zh: 我是Jill Robbins。

sentences.en: I'm Jonathan Evans.
sentences.zh: 我是Jonathan Evans。

sentences.en: And I'm John Russell.
sentences.zh: 我是John Russell。

glossary.def: grammar : a word or group of words added to a sentence to make it complete
grammar : a noun, pronoun, or noun phrase which indicates the person or thing that receives the action of a verb
a group of words that acts like a noun in a sentence
the thing that is being referred to
of, relating to, or having the function of an adverb
